tagline: Along the divide from South Hill to Pamplin City.
intro: Route 47 leaves South Hill westward on Atlantic Street and rides the drainage divide, the Meherrin River off to the north and the Roanoke to the south, through North View, Wightman and Drapersville to Chase City.

Past Craftons Gate it becomes Main Street in Drakes Branch, crosses Roanoke Creek to Charlotte Court House, and beyond the hamlet of Cullen it takes to the line between Charlotte and Prince Edward counties, running beside the railroad most of the way to Pamplin City.

moments.title: Chase City
moments.text: Incorporated in 1873, the town took its name from Salmon P. Chase, Lincoln's Secretary of the Treasury and a Chief Justice of the United States.

moments.title: Charlotte Court House
moments.text: Patrick Henry made his last political speech in the town in 1799, and its Jefferson-designed courthouse appeared in Sommersby, a film about the post-war South, shot here in 1992.

moments.title: Pamplin City
moments.text: A stop on the old Southside Railroad, the town keeps beside Business 460 the Pamplin Pipe Factory, once the largest clay pipe factory in the United States.
